Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.0.3

pytest 9.0.3 (2026-04-07)

Bug fixes

  • #12444: Fixed pytest.approx which now correctly takes into account ~collections.abc.Mapping keys order to compare them.

  • #13634: Blocking a conftest.py file using the -p no: option is now explicitly disallowed.

    Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

    Pytest now raises a clear UsageError explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via -p.

  • #13734: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with __tracebackhide__ = True.

  • #14195: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to unittest.TestCase.subTest() were not printed.

  • #14343: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).

Improved documentation

  • #13388: Clarified documentation for -p vs PYTEST_PLUGINS plugin loading and fixed an incorrect -p example.
  • #13731: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. capsys and capfd) take precedence over the -s / --capture=no command-line options in Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>.
  • #14088: Clarified that the default pytest_collection hook sets session.items before it calls pytest_collection_finish, not after.
  • #14255: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.

Contributor-facing changes

  • #12689: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions. The test statistics is visible on the web interface.

    -- by aleguy02

9.0.2

pytest 9.0.2 (2025-12-06)

Bug fixes

  • #13896: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

    You may enable it again by passing -p terminalprogress. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

    Additionally, when the environment variable TERM is dumb, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.

  • #13904: Fixed the TOML type of the tmp_path_retention_count settings in the API reference from number to string.

  • #13946: The private config.inicfg attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0. Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim. It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10.

subject: feat: Add insert notification methods and impl for all sql drivers (#578)
body:
This PR adds `enable_notify_insert`, `update_notify_insert`,
`disable_notify_insert`, and `list_notify_insert_throttles` methods to
the `Queue` trait and adds implementations for all the sql drivers we
support (sqlx, diesel, rust-postgres).

This PR also
- Replaces the `VisibilityTimeoutOffset` type with a new general
`Duration` type that can be used for both visibility timeout and insert
notification throttle interval parameters
- Changes the visibility of the SQL strings in `queue/sql` module to be
crate-private so we can change them if needed without breaking semver
- Uses `query_as` instead of `query` in the `sqlx` implementation where
possible (for methods with concrete, non-generic return types)
- Updates the relevant methods in `PGMQueueExt` to use the sqlx
implementation of `Queue`

The new tests in `tests/queue.rs` were copied from the existing tests in
`pg_ext_integration_test.rs` and translated to use the `Queue` trait
methods.

subject: feat: Add rust-postgres implementations of the `Queue` trait (#562)
body:
This PR adds implementations of the `Queue` trait for the `postgres` and
`tokio-postgres` crates. `postgres` is simply a synchronous wrapper
around the async `tokio-postgres` methods, so they can share a lot of
their functionality. In fact, the only differences are which connection
trait is used, one needs the connection/executor to be `&mut C` and one
can be `&C`, and one requires `await`-ing DB results. A custom macro is
used in order to generate the required code from the same shared logic.

Also:
- Because `sqlx` and the rust-postgres implementations use plain strings
for their queries, I pulled the strings out into shared constants.
- Add missing header type parameter for `Queue#read` method and
implementations

Relates to https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/425

subject: feat!: Initial `Queue` trait and `sqlx` implementation (#549)

Initial commit to add a new `Queue` trait to allow supporting multiple
different SQL clients (this PR only adds the `sqlx` implementation).

Some high-level details:

- The new `Queue` trait and implementations are in the `queue` mod
- Only three key methods are added initially: `create`, `send`, and
`read`
- Common implementation details exist in a macro, and individual
implementations are generated by invoking the macro with the relevant
parameters
- Added a `sqlx` feature flag for the `PGMQueueExt` client and the
`sqlx` implementation of the `Queue` trait
- Tests for all the implementations of the `Queue` trait are in the new
`queue` integration test file. Each implementation has a separate test
method generated for it using a new custom test macro.

Implementations for other clients (diesel/rust-postgres) will be added
in a separate followup PR.

Relates to https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/425

subject: chore: Check that upgrade scripts do not diverge from a fresh install (#525)
body:
## Problem
As seen in https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/521, it's easy for the
upgrade scripts to diverge from a fresh installation.

## Solution
This PR adds a check to verify that the upgrade scripts do not diverge
from a fresh installation. The check uses the output of `pg_dump` as
well as a manual query of the extensions functions (these are not
included in `pg_dump`).

This PR also adds a new migration script (`pgmq--1.11.0--1.11.1.sql`) to
resolve the existing differences between the upgrade scripts and a fresh
installation.

### Summary of differences and how they were resolved
#### `pgmq.read_grouped_head`

This function only existed in the fresh install (`pgmq.sql`), so this PR
adds it via a migration file as well.

#### `pgmq._ensure_pg_partman_installed`
This method exists for both fresh installs and upgrades, but the
implementations are different. This PR updates the version in the
upgrade path to match the fresh installation.

#### `enable_notify_insert`

This function ([added
here](https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/blob/66349cfee14ab75827eb541d36b2c84cbbb68dab/pgmq-extension/sql/pgmq--1.6.1--1.7.0.sql#L9))
originally had a single parameter but was [updated to have two
parameters](https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/blob/66349cfee14ab75827eb541d36b2c84cbbb68dab/pgmq-extension/sql/pgmq--1.7.1--1.8.0.sql#L45)
-- the single-parameter version does not exist in fresh installs. I'm
guessing that the upgrade script was intending to replace the
single-parameter version with the two-parameter version, but `CREATE OR
REPLACE FUNCTION` does not replace an existing function if the parameter
types are different, even if the function names match, so the
single-parameter version was not removed.

This PR removes the single parameter version. This should not be a
breaking change as the two-parameter version has a default value for the
second parameter, so it can be called in the same way as the old
single-parameter version.

#### `pg_dump` output
First, there was a missing `PERFORM
pg_catalog.pg_extension_config_dump('pgmq.topic_bindings', '');` call
for the migration path. This PR adds the missing call.

Second, in the migration path, the `pgmq.notify_insert_throttle` and
`pgmq.topic_bindings` tables are created after the blanket `GRANT`s from
the fresh installation script, so they each have an extra `GRANT SELECT

subject: fix: Race condition in `PGMQueueExt#create` (#520)
body:
Problem
-------
`PGMQueueExt#create` is supposed to return `Ok(false)` if the queue was
not created (e.g., it already exists). However, the check for whether
the queue exists is performed without any locking. This means it's
possible for two processes to call `PGMQueueExt#create` at the same time
and both get an `Ok(true)` response. This can (usually) be seen in the
negative test case added in this PR -- it may not always happen due to
the non-deterministic nature of race conditions.

Solution
--------
Create a transaction to perform all DB operations in, and call
`pgmq.acquire_queue_lock` for the queue before checking if it exists.
This is the same function called by `pgmq.create` before it creates the
queue (we don't need to worry about lock contention for the same
transaction).

Here’s an example of the test failing (the commit tested here did not
have the fix):
https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/actions/runs/23983765959/job/69952299454?pr=520#step:7:880

subject: fix: Race condition in `PGMQueueExt#init` (#519)
body:
Problem
-------
When multiple processes attempt to run
`PGMQueueExt#init`/`PGMQueueExt#init_with_cxn` at the same time, the
following error is seen:

```
failed to init pgmq: DatabaseError(Database(PgDatabaseError { severity: Error, code: "23505", message: "duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"pg_namespace_nspname_index\"", detail: Some("Key (nspname)=(pgmq) already exists."), hint: None, position: None, where: None, schema: Some("pg_catalog"), table: Some("pg_namespace"), column: None, data_type: None, constraint: Some("pg_namespace_nspname_index"), file: Some("nbtinsert.c"), line: Some(666), routine: Some("_bt_check_unique") }))
```

This can be easily reproduced by running `pg_ext_integration_test`
without the initialization steps provided in `make test`:

```shell
make run.postgres && sleep 2 && cargo test --test pg_ext_integration_test
```

Solution
--------
This PR resolves the race condition by acquiring a transaction-level
advisory lock before attempting to create the extension. This is the
same approach used by the SQL-only installation method.

This PR also adds a check to CI to run the extension tests without
initializing the extension first to confirm that the race condition does
not exist and is not re-introduced later. Here's an example failure (the
commit tested here did not acquire the lock):
https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/actions/runs/23958025280/job/69881120612?pr=519#step:6:498

subject: feat!: Improve sql-only installation from the Rust client (#508)
body:
## Problem
As described in https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/504, the current
SQL-only installation method is not ideal for production use because

1. It fetches the installation script from GitHub, which can introduce
instability into a service that runs the installation during boot along
with its other migrations.
2. There's no guarantee that the installed version is compatible with
the current version of the `pgmq` client.
3. The installation is not versioned, making it difficult to upgrade
`pgmq` to a new version.
4. There is no locking mechanism, so if multiple processes attempt to
install `pgmq` at the same time, they may conflict and fail to install


## Solution
This PR solves the above problems for the Rust client. It does so by:

1. Adding a new installation method that uses SQL scripts that are
embedded into the `pgmq` crate, eliminating the need to download the
scripts from GitHub at runtime. This also means that the Rust client
will always install the latest version of `pgmq` that it's compatible
with.
2. Tracking which migration scripts were run in a table managed by the
Rust client, along with the version associated with each script. This
allows upgrading `pgmq` by running all migrations greater than the last
run migration.
3. Using locks to ensure that only a single process can run the SQL-only
installation at once. This approach will work across different client
implementations as long as they use the same locks (one advisory lock
and one table-level lock).

All of the above is implemented with pure-PostgreSQL functionality, so
it should be easy to implement in other clients.

This PR also:
1. Updates the `crate_ci.yml` and `extension_upgrade.yml` workflows to
ensure the SQL-only installation is tested just as thoroughly as the
extension installation.
2. Adds a utility method to initialize the "applied migrations" table to
enable switching from the previous unversioned SQL-only installation
method to the new versioned method(s). This is required for the use case
described in https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/514)
3. Adds a utility method to fetch the currently installed version of
PGMQ (assuming it was installed with the new versioned SQL-only method).

Closes https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/504
Closes https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq/issues/417

subject: feat!: Allow using more Rust types for `delay`/`vt` in `PGMQueueExt` (#515)
body:
Problem
-------
Currently, `PGMQueueExt` only accepts integer types for the `vt`/`delay`
parameters of its methods. This is inconvenient, particularly because
the `std::time::Duration#as_secs` method returns a `u64`, so a cast is
required in order to call these methods. It's also slightly unclear
whether the `vt` parameter refers to a delay or a timestamp (as an epoch
timestamp).

Solution
--------
Create a `VisibilityTimeoutOffset` "new type" to wrap the offset value
in seconds as an `i32`. Provide default implementations from various
integer types, `std::time::Duration`, and `chrono::Duration`, and cap
the value to `i32::MIN`/`i32::MIN` if an overflow would occur during
conversion.

Note:
- I think this is technically a semver breaking change. While most
usages shouldn't break, it would probably break if someone was using
implicit type detection with a `try_into()` call.

* fix: Override types of timestamp columns to avoid `time` conflict

Problem
-------
If a consumer has both the `time` and `chrono` features of `sqlx`
enabled, `sqlx` will default to using `OffsetDateTime` (from `time`)
for timestamp fields instead of `DateTime<Utc>` (from `chrono`).
It's easy to accidentally encounter this situation, either by directly
enabling `time`, e.g., if the consumer prefers `time` over `chrono`, or
if the `time` feature is enabled by a transitive dependency. When this
situation occurs, the `pg_ext::PGMQueueMeta` struct can not be built
from the sqlx query because an `OffsetDateTime` was returned instead of
a `DateTime<Utc>`, causing a compile error.

Solution
--------
`sqlx` provides a way to override the type of an output column:
https://docs.rs/sqlx/latest/sqlx/macro.query.html#force-a-differentcustom-type.
Update the failing queries in the `pg_ext` to use this approach.
Unfortunately, I think this requires using the more verbose approach of
naming each column to be returned instead of using `*`.

Testing
-------
- I ran the examples and they appeared to run successfully
- I enabled the `time` feature of `sqlx` in the `dev-dependencies` to
  ensure this case of enabling `chrono` and `time` is supported, which
  can be confirmed by compiling examples/tests.

Other
-----
I also updated the sqlx query caches. I noticed there was an unused
column called `headers` in some of the queries that used a `*` selector.
I can add the column back, but it didn't appear to be used, so I left it
out.
